headline: Implicit Social Cognition · Greenwald & Banaji 1995
quote: Implicit attitudes are introspectively unidentified (or inaccurately identified) traces of past experience that mediate favorable or unfavorable feeling, thought, or action toward social objects.
attribution: Anthony G. Greenwald & Mahzarin R. Banaji, Psychological Review 102(1), 1995, p. 8
